newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's ONGC revises 96/97 crude output target.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC revises 96/97 crude output target.

text.p: India's government-approved crude production target for state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd has been revised to 30.5 million tonnes for the fiscal year 1996/97 (April-March), a company spokesman said on Thursday.
Included in that is a a reduced target for Bombay High Basin production of 20.5 million tonnes, down 1.5 million tonnes from the previous target, the spokesman said.
ONGC is India's main crude producer at more than 90 percent of the country's output.
The government set ONGC's first overall target at 34.5 million tonnes.
But ONGC has been using a lower estimate around 29.5 million tonnes for most of the year due to falling production at the offshore Bombay High Basin, the country's main producing area.
Last week, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas set the latest target as it did not approve of the lower estimate for a target, the spokesman said.
In the last fiscal year, ONGC produced a total of nearly 32 million tonnes of crude, of which 22.6 miilion was produced from the Bombay High Basin.

In the latest production figures, 20.979 million tonnes of crude were produced in the first nine months of the current fiscal year, a fall of around two million tonnes compared with the same period in the last fiscal year.
Bombay High output has fallen steadily for the last nine months and produced only 15.236 million tonnes in the nine month period compared with 17.137 million tonnes year-on-year.
